text: Aralle-Tabulahan is an Austronesian language classified within the South Sulawesi subgroup and is spoken in Mamasa Regency, West Sulawesi, Indonesia. It has three primary dialects: Aralle, Tabulahan, and Mambi. The Mambi dialect is considered the most divergent among the three and is positioned at the center of the dialect spectrum, lying between the Aralle and Tabulahan dialects and the related Bambam language.
